model.name: Software Component / Package
model.purpose: Capture versioned distributable dependency identity so an agent can identify, classify, locate, verify, relate and govern a software package independently of storage format.
model.scope_statement: This model is the format-neutral record of a versioned, distributable software component or package: the identity coordinates used to name it, the version and release state, the type or purpose, the bits and locators that constitute a distribution, cryptographic integrity, declared origin and rights, and the typed dependency and containment edges needed to treat it as a reusable dependency. It is not the software product offering, not the SBOM document, and not an installed configuration item.
in_scope: Canonical and ecosystem-native identity for a versioned package, including Package-URL, registry coordinates, CPE class names, SWID tag identifiers, SPDX element IRIs, and content-addressed identifiers such as SWHID, gitoid and hashes
Version strings and version schemes, including pre-release, build metadata, snapshots, classifiers and the immutability rule for a released version
Component type, software purpose and packaging or media of the distributable
Download, homepage and repository locators, including PURL qualifiers that select repository, architecture or distro
Cryptographic hashes, signatures and independent recomputation of content identifiers
Direct dependency, optional, provided, static/dynamic link and containment relationships, including known unknowns
Originator, supplier, manufacturer, publisher and namespace publication authority
Declared and concluded license identifiers and copyright text as package metadata, not as a full license model
Release, yank, deprecate, support-level and validity-window lifecycle
Access class, retention after withdrawal, and mappings among identifier systems
out_of_scope: The software product or service offering as a commercial or operational whole, which belongs to WM-SFT-001
The SBOM or BOM document, serial number, document author and document timestamp as a first-class inventory artifact, which belong to WM-SFT-012
Individual files, snippets and source-tree objects as standalone entities, except as referenced containment or content identifiers
Vulnerability, advisory, VEX and CVE records
License legal text, license exceptions, obligations and compliance determinations beyond identifiers asserted on the package
Build recipes, SLSA provenance, CI run identity and compiler toolchain as a process model
Hardware devices, HWID tags and physical parts
AI model cards, training datasets and SaaS runtime service identity as distinct models
Package-manager user interfaces, registry implementation internals and transport protocols
Installed-on-device configuration items as IT asset instances, except where a SWID primary or patch tag is used as an aligned identifier for the same software class

boundary_notes.distinction: A product is composed of one or more versioned packages; this model is the constituent distributable identity, not the product's commercial, contractual or service envelope.

An SBOM is an inventory document that lists packages and relationships; this model is one listed component. Package records may reference an SBOM, but document serial numbers, SBOM author and SBOM capture lifecycle belong to the SBOM model.
SPDX treats Package as a unit of distribution that typically contains files; files and snippets remain separable SoftwareArtifact subclasses and should not be collapsed into the package identity.
This model records declared, concluded and observed license identifiers and copyright text on the package. License texts, exceptions and legal interpretation belong to a composable license model.
PURL, CPE and SWID are used to match vulnerabilities to packages, but the vulnerability record, scoring and VEX status are not package attributes.

CPE names abstract product classes, not unique installations. SWID primary and patch tags describe installed or patched copies. This model centres on the distributable package used as a dependency, and treats installation tags as aligned identifiers rather than the master entity.
builtTime, downloadLocation and supplier describe the package; the build process, builder identity and provenance attestation are a sibling process model.

bundles.name: Identity and coordinates
bundles.description: How a versioned package is named and disambiguated across registries, class dictionaries and content-addressed schemes.
bundles.rationale: Package identity is the operating core of this model: without a defensible coordinate, dependency resolution, vulnerability matching and SBOM joining fail. Multiple identifier families coexist and must be recorded without collapsing their semantics.

layers.name: Universal and dictionary identifiers
layers.description: PURL, SPDX element IRI, CPE class names, SWID tags and content-addressed identifiers that are intended to work across tools.

findings.name: Package-URL identity
findings.description: A Package-URL (PURL) is a URL-based identifier with scheme pkg, a type, optional namespace, name, optional version, qualifiers and subpath, used to identify and locate a software package independently of a single ecosystem's native string.

questions.text: What is the canonical Package-URL for this package version?
answer_data: Canonical PURL string in the form scheme:type/namespace/name@version?qualifiers#subpath
Canonicalization notes such as removal of pkg:// authority slashes

questions.text: Which PURL type, namespace, name, version, qualifiers and subpath were parsed from that identifier?
answer_data: PURL type code such as maven, npm, pypi, deb, rpm, golang, nuget, cargo or generic
Namespace, name, version, qualifier map and subpath

questions.text: How does this PURL map to the ecosystem-native registry coordinate used by the authoritative package manager?
answer_data: Registry or type-definition rule used for the mapping

questions.text: Which qualifiers select a specific binary, repository mirror, architecture, distro or packaging that is not implied by name and version alone?
answer_data: Qualifier keys and values such as arch, distro, repository_url, packaging, classifier or vers
Whether those qualifiers are required for uniqueness in this type

findings.description: CPE names identify abstract product classes; SWID tags identify software products and lifecycle roles; SPDX spdxId is the element IRI inside an SPDX graph. These identifiers coexist with PURL and must not be treated as equivalent.

part, vendor, product, version, update and other WFN attributes

findings.name: Content-addressed identifiers
findings.description: SWHID, gitoid and cryptographic hashes identify artifacts by what they are, not by where they are registered. They remain stable if a registry name is transferred or a download URL dies, and they can be recomputed by anyone who has the bits.

answer_data: SWHID string such as swh:1:cnt:… or swh:1:rel:…

answer_data: Which payload was hashed (archive, directory tree, file)

If a gitoid is present, is it recorded as a SoftwareArtifact contentIdentifier or as an Element externalIdentifier for an OmniBOR input manifest?

bundles.name: Version, classification and lifecycle
bundles.description: What the package is, which incarnation it is, and whether that incarnation is still the intended dependency.
bundles.rationale: Version identity is not a date. Classification drives how the package is used in composition. Lifecycle distinguishes released, snapshot, pre-release, yanked and unsupported copies.

layers.name: Versioning and compatibility
layers.description: Version strings, schemes, precedence, pre-release and the immutability contract of a released version.

findings.name: Version identity and scheme
findings.description: A package version is an opaque-or-structured string whose meaning depends on the scheme. SemVer defines MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, pre-release and build metadata and forbids modifying a released version. Maven versions include SNAPSHOT and classifiers. Ecosystem versions (Debian epochs, PEP 440, CalVer) may differ. CycloneDX and SPDX treat version as optional even though SBOM minimum-element guidance treats it as baseline.

questions.text: What version string identifies this released or pre-release package?
answer_data: Whether version is absent and why

questions.text: Which version scheme is used to parse and compare this version string?
answer_data: Scheme code such as semver-2, maven, pep440, debian, calver, ecosystem-native or unknown

questions.text: Has the content associated with this version been modified after the version was released, in violation of SemVer immutability or registry policy?
answer_data: Evidence of mutation such as hash change at same version

questions.text: Is this version a pre-release, snapshot, build-metadata-only variant, or a stable release, and how does that affect precedence?
answer_data: Precedence notes versus the associated normal version

questions.text: When was this version released or built, and when was that version metadata observed or ingested?
answer_data: releaseTime as RFC 3339 with seconds and offset
observation or ingestion time if distinct from event time

findings.inline_only_rationale: Version strings, scheme codes and immutability flags are inline metadata. They are not documents; the immutable payload they name is the package archive.

layers.name: Type and purpose
layers.description: Classification of the package by CycloneDX component type and SPDX software purpose, which describe use context as well as content.

findings.name: Component type and software purpose
findings.description: CycloneDX requires a component type such as application, library, framework, container, operating-system, firmware, file or machine-learning-model. SPDX records primaryPurpose and additionalPurpose, noting that purpose is intrinsic to how the element is used rather than solely to its content. The two vocabularies overlap but are not identical.

questions.text: What CycloneDX component type classifies this package?
answer_data: Fallback rule if classified as application because no more specific type applies

questions.text: What SPDX primaryPurpose and additionalPurpose values describe how this package is used?
Is the recorded purpose based on use context rather than bit content, and could the same bits be a library in one product and an application in another?

data_elements.description: Required type in CycloneDX component records.

data_elements.description: Primary SoftwarePurpose of the package.

data_elements.description: Additional SoftwarePurpose values.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Type and purpose are classifier codes on the package record. They are not independent artifacts.

layers.name: Release state and support
layers.description: Publication, withdrawal, support level and validity windows, including SWID corpus/primary/patch roles.

findings.name: Release lifecycle and support
findings.description: A package version is published, may be yanked or retracted while remaining resolvable, may be deprecated, and may carry supportLevel and validUntilTime. CycloneDX BOM lifecycles (design through decommission) describe when inventory was captured, which is observation context rather than the package's own release state. SWID distinguishes corpus, primary, patch and supplemental tags across the software lifecycle.

answer_data: Whether it describes installation media, an installed copy, a patch or supplemental metadata

questions.text: Has this package version been scheduled for decommission or retirement from operations?
answer_data: Decommission flag or CycloneDX decommission lifecycle presence

bundles.description: Where the bits live and how their integrity is verified.
bundles.rationale: A coordinate without locatable, hash-verified bits cannot be operated as a dependency. Locators and hashes are complementary: URLs move, digests do not.

findings.description: SPDX Hash requires algorithm and hashValue as an IntegrityMethod on verifiedUsing. CycloneDX records an array of component hashes. findings.name: Dependency relationships
findings.description: SPDX dependsOn, hasOptionalDependency, hasProvidedDependency, hasPrerequisite, hasStaticLink and hasDynamicLink relate packages during a lifecycle scope. CycloneDX component scope is required, optional or excluded. Maven scopes include compile, provided, runtime, test and system, plus optional and version requirement specifications. Transitive closure is derived, not an identity. Incomplete graphs should record known unknowns.

CycloneDX metadata.component and compositions describe the root and relationship completeness. The SBOM document is WM-SFT-012; this package references it rather than embedding document identity as its own identity.

Organization address, when present, is the only spatial attribute commonly attached to a package.

CycloneDX licenses may be declared or concluded, with observed licenses under evidence. copyrightText and attributionText are package-level assertions. This is identifier-level metadata, not a substitute for a license instrument model.

layers.name: Access, retention and interoperability
layers.description: Who may use the record and the bits, what remains after yank or deletion, and how identifier systems are aligned without false conformance.

findings.name: Access, retention and identifier interoperability
findings.description: Private registries, embargoed versions and export controls constrain access to bits even when metadata is visible. Yank, unpublish and delete policies differ by ecosystem and often leave a resolvable tombstone. PURL, CPE, SWID, SPDX IRI and hashes answer different identity questions; mapping is an alignment, not identity equality. VERS version-range syntax is emerging and is not yet an Ecma standard.

Deletion event time versus observation time

functions.name: Resolve package identity
functions.description: Given a native coordinate, PURL, CPE, SWID, hash or Dimension id, resolve to a single package record and its identifier map.
preconditions: At least one identifier is supplied
Identifier syntax is parseable for its claimed type
effects: Reads but does not mutate package records
May record an observation time for the resolution event

functions.name: Verify package integrity
functions.description: Compute digests of a local payload and compare them to publisher-declared hashes or a SWHID.
inputs: Package record identifier or payload bytes
preconditions: At least one declared IntegrityMethod or SWHID exists
effects: Records verification result and verification time distinct from releaseTime

functions.name: List direct dependencies
functions.description: Return typed dependency edges for a package, including scope and known unknowns, without implying a complete transitive closure unless requested.
outputs: Edge list with relationship type and scope
effects: Reads dependency declarations and lockfile-derived edges
Does not invent missing transitive nodes

functions.name: Compare package versions
functions.description: Order two version strings under a declared scheme and report precedence, including pre-release handling.
inputs: Optional PURL type for ecosystem rules
outputs: Whether they are comparable under the scheme
Notes on build metadata being ignored for SemVer precedence
preconditions: A version scheme is declared or defaulted with an explicit warning
effects: Pure comparison with no registry mutation

functions.name: Map external identifiers
functions.description: Translate among PURL, native coordinates, CPE and SWID without claiming that a successful map is identity equality.
outputs: Explicit non-map when CPE class cannot select a unique PURL
effects: Writes or updates the identifier alignment map when a mapping is stored
Must record conflicts rather than overwrite

functions.name: Publish package release
functions.description: Register a new immutable version of a package with native coordinates, hashes and optional PURL.
outputs: Assigned PURL if type rules exist
preconditions: Publisher is authorized for the namespace
Version has not already been released with different bits
Hashes of the payload are present or computable
effects: Sets content immutability to true for non-snapshot versions

functions.name: Withdraw or yank a release
functions.description: Mark a published version yanked, deprecated or unpublished according to policy without silently recycling the version string.
preconditions: Action is allowed by the registry or Dimension policy
effects: Does not reuse the version string for different bits
May retain bits or only metadata per retention policy
Records event time and observation time separately

composition.purpose: A software product is composed of versioned packages; this package record is referenced as a constituent rather than absorbing the product envelope.
A package or release references one or more SBOM documents that inventory it; SBOM document identity stays in the SBOM model.
Align field semantics with the SPDX Package class and SoftwareArtifact properties without claiming document-level SPDX conformance.
Align component type, purl, hashes, licenses, scope, supplier and dependency graph with CycloneDX component semantics.
Use PURL as the governed cross-ecosystem identifier syntax.
Record CPE names as class identifiers for vulnerability and inventory matching, not as unique package instance identifiers.
Align SWID tag identity and lifecycle roles where an installation or corpus tag exists for the same software.
Align content-addressed identity and independent integrity verification.
Align version grammar, precedence and released-version immutability when the package declares SemVer.
Align Java-ecosystem master-system coordinates, classifiers, packaging and dependency scopes.
Package records point at license identifiers; they do not own license text or obligations.
Packages are matched to vulnerabilities via PURL or CPE; vulnerability state lives elsewhere.

owner_package_requirements: The software product or service owner accountable for the package namespace must be recorded, even when originator and supplier differ.
Each Dimension instance must declare which ecosystem registries it treats as master systems for native coordinates.
Owner packages must bind at least one integrity method (hash or SWHID) before a non-snapshot version is marked released.
Owner packages must not present JSON, YAML, Git or MongoDB layout as the semantic model.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use the PURL type as the ecosystem axis and the native group or scope as the namespace axis. SPDX alignments may use the Package class IRI https://spdx.org/rdf/3.0.1/terms/Software/Package. Dimension-local record ids are lower-kebab-case or ULID/UUID and must not embed dates. Do not treat a version string or release date as an identifier.
registry_links: ECMA-427 / Package-URL type index at https://www.packageurl.org/docs/purl/introduction and https://github.com/package-url/purl-spec

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize PURLs per ECMA-427: scheme pkg with a single colon, no pkg:// authority, type-specific encoding of namespace and name.
Prefer digest-based identifiers over mutable tags for container and similar ecosystems.
Store native coordinates un-lossy even when a PURL is also present.
Treat CPE 2.2 URI and CPE 2.3 formatted string as bindings of one WFN, not as two products.
Normalize timestamps to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.
patch_rules: A released non-snapshot version MUST NOT have its payload bytes patched in place; issue a new version.
Metadata-only patches (yank flag, supplier correction, additional hashes, identifier maps) increment a record revision distinct from package version.
Conflicting identifier assertions are appended with provenance rather than silently replaced.
License conclusion updates do not overwrite declared licenses.
compatibility_rules: SPDX 3.x is a breaking revision relative to SPDX 2.3 / ISO/IEC 5962:2021; map fields explicitly and do not claim 2.3 conformance from 3.x records.
CycloneDX component version is optional since 1.4; consumers that require NTIA/CISA baseline version must treat missing version as incomplete, not as version zero.
SemVer 2.0.0 and Maven version comparison are not interchangeable; Maven coordinate guidance currently points at SemVer 1.0.0.
PURL type definitions may evolve under the Package-URL project even while ECMA-427 core syntax is stable; record the type-definition version used.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: the native package coordinate assigned by the ecosystem's authoritative registry or package manager (for example Maven groupId:artifactId:version with classifier and extension when required, or the registry name and version for npm, PyPI, NuGet, crates.io and equivalent ecosystems).
Governed global identifier or IRI: a canonical Package-URL per ECMA-427, and when present an SPDX Package element IRI (spdxId).
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when no registry coordinate or PURL can yet be established.
Content-addressed identifiers (SWHID, gitoid, payload hashes) corroborate identity but do not replace the master-system coordinate when one exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values SHALL be recorded as RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z. Record event time (builtTime, releaseTime, yank or deprecation time, verification time) separately from observation or ingestion time whenever those differ; a BOM or harvest timestamp is observation time, not the package release event.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named from the master-system coordinate plus a role suffix (manifest, archive, checksum, swid, lockfile, signature) and MUST include a content digest in their identity; dates and mutable tags MUST NOT be the sole name.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every stored archive SHOULD have at least one cryptographically strong digest (SHA-256 or stronger, or a SWHID) computed or verified at ingestion; publisher-declared and Dimension-computed digests are stored as distinct values so mismatches remain visible.

policies: Released non-snapshot payload immutability: never recycle a version string for different bits.
Known unknowns in dependency graphs MUST be explicit; absence of an edge is not evidence of independence.
Identifier mappings are alignments; do not claim CPE, PURL, SWID or SPDX conformance without recorded evidence.
Namespace transfer or maintainer change requires an authority record and leaves prior versions' originator history intact.
Private, embargoed or export-controlled packages default to deny on bit download even if metadata is internally visible.
CISA/NTIA baseline component fields (supplier, name, version, other identifiers, dependency relationship) are treated as completeness targets, not as proof that a given SBOM document is compliant.

read: Resolve by native coordinate, PURL, hash, SWID tagId, CPE name or Dimension id.
List versions of a name including yanked tombstones unless a policy hides them.
Return identifier maps, hashes and dependency edges with completeness flags.
create: Publish a new version only when the actor is namespace-authorized and hashes are present.
Create Dimension-local records for observed packages that lack a registry coordinate, assigning a ULID/UUID.
Ingest registry metadata with an observation time distinct from releaseTime.
update: Allow metadata-only updates: additional identifiers, hash corroboration, yank/deprecate flags, license conclusions, supplier corrections.
Forbid in-place payload mutation for immutable versions; require fn-publish-release for bit changes.
Record the patch actor and patch observation time.
delete: Prefer yank or unpublish tombstones over hard delete so that the version string remains reserved.
Hard delete of bits or metadata follows the recorded retention policy and legal hold exceptions.
Deletion event time and the observation of deletion are both recorded.

roles.name: Software product or service owner
responsibilities: Accountable for the package as a constituent of WM-SFT-001
Approves namespace ownership and public release policy

roles.name: Package maintainer or publisher
responsibilities: Assigns version numbers and publishes artifacts
Declares licenses, originator data and dependency manifests

roles.name: Registry operator
responsibilities: Enforces yank, unpublish and namespace-transfer rules

roles.name: SBOM or composition analyst
responsibilities: Records known unknowns and relationship completeness

roles.name: Security and SCA consumer
responsibilities: Matches PURL and CPE to vulnerability intelligence

roles.name: Dimension steward
responsibilities: Governs canonicalization, access scopes and retention

access.default_rule: Metadata of public registry packages is readable to authenticated Dimension users; payload bytes follow the originating registry's public-or-private class, defaulting to deny for internal, embargoed or unsigned packages until an integrity check is recorded.
exceptions: Embargoed pre-releases visible only to named maintainer and owner roles
Private-feed packages never exported through public interfaces
Legal hold that blocks yank deletion despite maintainer request
Export-control or license-restricted binaries whose metadata may be listed without enabling download
audit_requirements: Log resolve, publish, verify, yank and identifier-map writes with actor, event time and observation time.
Retain integrity verification outcomes even when the archive is later deleted.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md for Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before any other Dimension file.
Read identifier, version and integrity findings before dependency or license findings.
Treat JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git, MCP and MongoDB as projections listed by Storage type URL and Interface URL, not as the model.

coverage.claim: This structure is a defensible, format-neutral operating context for versioned distributable software component and package identity, grounded in SPDX 3.0.1, ECMA-427 PURL, CycloneDX 1.6, NIST CPE 2.3, ISO/IEC 19770-2 SWID, ISO/IEC 18670 SWHID, SemVer 2.0.0, Maven POM coordinates and CISA SBOM framing. It is not a claim of universal completeness or of conformance to any one SBOM standard.

checklist.notes: Master-system native coordinates, PURL, SPDX IRI, CPE, SWID, SWHID, gitoid and Dimension ULID/UUID are modelled with an explicit priority and class-versus-instance distinction.
Release, pre-release, snapshot, yank, deprecate, supportLevel, validUntilTime, SWID tag roles and decommission intent are included.
dependsOn and related SPDX types, CycloneDX/Maven scopes, containment, pedigree, SBOM and product links are included.
builtTime, releaseTime, validUntilTime, verification time and observation or ingestion time are distinguished under an RFC 3339 rule.
originatedBy, manufacturer, retrieval source, pedigree and identity-assertion evidence are included; full SLSA build provenance is out of scope.
Namespace owner, publisher, supplier versus originator, and copyright text are included.
Hash verification, PURL canonical form, version immutability and identifier mapping lossiness are included.
Public versus authenticated versus internal distribution, metadata versus bit-download, and embargo exceptions are included.

Yank tombstones, unpublish versus hard delete, version-string reservation and legal-hold exceptions are included; ecosystem-specific unpublish windows are not all cited from primary registry policies.
PURL, CPE, SWID, SPDX, CycloneDX and Maven alignments are explicit; conflicts are recorded rather than papered over.
CycloneDX component type and SPDX SoftwarePurpose are both captured, with a note that purpose is use-context.
Declared versus computed hashes, SWHID recomputation and optional signatures are included.
Declared, concluded and observed license identifiers plus copyright text; legal instruments remain a sibling model.
Scheme, pre-release, build metadata, SNAPSHOT mutability and SemVer immutability are included. VERS ranges are an emerging omission.

known_omissions: The CISA 2026 Minimum Elements PDF body was not retrieved; field-level 2026 deltas versus NTIA 2021 are therefore not cited as primary text.
VERS version-range syntax is planned as an Ecma standard in 2026 and is not treated as normative here.
Ecosystem-specific version grammars beyond SemVer and Maven (PEP 440, Debian Policy epochs, RubyGems, NuGet, Go modules, OCI index, conda, Hex, Yocto) are not fully expanded.
Registry unpublish windows (npm, crates.io yank, PyPI yank) lack first-party policy citations in this pass.
EU Cyber Resilience Act component identification duties, NIST SSDF, and sector SBOM profiles are not incorporated.
Sigstore/Rekor, in-toto and SLSA provenance attestations are omitted as a sibling process model.
OSGi bundle symbolic-name+version, Java module names, and language-level package names distinct from distribution packages are omitted.
Private coordinate collisions across disconnected registries (same GAV, different bits) need operational federation rules not specified by the cited standards.
conflicts: CPE identifies abstract product classes, not unique package instantiations or installations (NIST CPE 2.3 versus PURL/SWID).
SPDX 3.0.1 is a breaking model relative to SPDX 2.3 / ISO/IEC 5962:2021.
CycloneDX and SPDX make package version optional; CISA/NTIA framing treats component version as a baseline SBOM attribute.
SemVer 2.0.0 forbids modifying released content; Maven SNAPSHOT versions and mutable container tags intentionally violate that immutability.
Apache Maven coordinate guidance recommends Semantic Versioning 1.0.0, not 2.0.0.
SPDX SoftwarePurpose and CycloneDX component type overlap but are not a 1:1 code set; purpose is use-context in SPDX.
Declared versus concluded licenses may disagree; neither is the legal instrument.
The same bits may be published under multiple PURLs (mirrors, forks, republished Maven coordinates), so PURL uniqueness is per ecosystem coordinate, not per content.
CISA 2026 replaces NTIA 2021 minimum elements at guidance level while Framing 2024 remains the detailed attribute discussion; do not claim a single current field table without the 2026 PDF.
regional_assumptions: US CISA/NTIA SBOM guidance is treated as influential public-authority practice, not as global law.
English remains the normative language of SPDX.
Public default registries (Maven Central, npmjs.com, PyPI) are used as examples of master systems; many enterprises use internal registries as the true master.
ISO SWID and SWHID are international; operational SWID issuance is uneven outside US federal software identification programmes.
adversarial_checks: Mutable container or Git tags presented as versions must lose to digest or SWHID identity, or the record is incomplete.
Namespace hijack or coordinate reuse after unpublish must not silently attach new bits to an old version string.
A CPE match must not be treated as proof that this exact package instance is affected.
Publisher-declared hashes that disagree with ingestion-time hashes must remain visible rather than averaged.
Dual publication of the same archive under two PURLs must produce two coordinates with a same-content relationship, not a merged identity.
Missing dependency edges must not be interpreted as an empty graph when completeness is unknown.
